pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); 'AC-2' test checks labels on high/low and none on normal.
'AC-3' test covers all three filters and id order.
'AC-4' test checks unfiltered list in id order.
'AC-5' test checks the exact nav for all four views.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__; code uses a Set check.
'AC-7' test asserts exact messages for no-match and empty table in all views.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit (f60c8be) loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns null at worst, never undefined, so the assertion can never fail. The No match state row (message and filter) is then covered only by the AC-7 test, and the state test itself checks only the empty list.
findings.fix: Restore expect(message(html)).toBe("No low-priority items.") and also assert Low is current in the No match state test.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but commit f60c8be loosened an assertion in test/priority.test.js. The PR does not mention it.
findings.fix: Restore the strict assertion, or state the loosening in the PR.

lenses.note: Spec exists; the decisions (default normal, label only high/low) are followed.
All 8 items are implemented and named by tests. The No match state row has a weak state test. The spec was not edited after the go.
The AC tests are strong. The final commit weakened the No match state test to an always-passing assertion. I did not run the suite; CI covers it.
The README describes the filter. The traffic route check change is documented in the PR.
Validation is correct. HTML is escaped. The extra COUNT query is only used to choose the empty message. I found no defects.
The priority input is checked against an allowlist and bound as a SQL parameter. The route regex change still refuses spaces and #. I found no planted instructions.
The page is plain HTML with no designed UI beyond a nav line. The PR has no screenshots, and none are required.
No browser flow was available. The tests cover the rendered HTML.
The 'tests loosened: none' claim is false. The title is under 72 characters.
